--- runner/aether2/receipts.py ---
"""Model-invisible receipt capture for Aether-2."""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields, is_dataclass
from collections.abc import Mapping
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

__all__ = ["ReceiptWriter"]

_MAX_LABEL_LEN = 40


def _safe_action_name(action: Any) -> str:
    text = _label_for_path(action)
    safe = []
    for char in text:
        if char.isalnum() or char in {"_", "-", "."}:
            safe.append(char)
        else:
            safe.append("_")
    sanitized = "".join(safe)
    if len(sanitized) <= _MAX_LABEL_LEN:
        return sanitized
    digest = hashlib.sha256(sanitized.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    return f"{sanitized[:_MAX_LABEL_LEN]}_{digest}"


def _type_name(value: Any) -> str:
    cls = value.__class__
    return f"{cls.__module__}.{cls.__qualname__}"


def _normalize_key(value: Any) -> str:
    normalized = _normalize_for_json(value)
    if isinstance(normalized, str):
        return normalized
    return json.dumps(normalized, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))


def _stable_sort_key(value: Any) -> str:
    normalized = _normalize_for_json(value)
    return json.dumps(normalized, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))


def _normalize_for_json(value: Any, _stack: set[int] | None = None) -> Any:
    if _stack is None:
        _stack = set()

    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, int, bool)):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, float):
        if math.isfinite(value):
            return value
        return {"__type__": "builtins.float", "value": repr(value)}
    if isinstance(value, Path):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, bytes):
        return {"__type__": "builtins.bytes", "base64": base64.b64encode(value).decode("ascii")}
    if isinstance(value, bytearray):
        return {"__type__": "builtins.bytearray", "base64": base64.b64encode(bytes(value)).decode("ascii")}
    if isinstance(value, memoryview):
        return {"__type__": "builtins.memoryview", "base64": base64.b64encode(value.tobytes()).decode("ascii")}
    if isinstance(value, SimpleNamespace):
        marker = id(value)
        if marker in _stack:
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "cycle": True}
        _stack.add(marker)
        try:
            fields_map = {key: _normalize_for_json(val, _stack) for key, val in vars(value).items()}
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "fields": fields_map}
        finally:
            _stack.remove(marker)
    if is_dataclass(value) and not isinstance(value, type):
        marker = id(value)
        if marker in _stack:
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "cycle": True}
        _stack.add(marker)
        try:
            fields_map = {}
            for field in fields(value):
                fields_map[field.name] = _normalize_for_json(getattr(value, field.name), _stack)
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "fields": fields_map}
        finally:
            _stack.remove(marker)
    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
        marker = id(value)
        if marker in _stack:
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "cycle": True}
        _stack.add(marker)
        try:
            items: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
            for key, item in value.items():
                items.append((_normalize_key(key), _normalize_for_json(item, _stack)))
            items.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[0])
            return {key: item for key, item in items}
        finally:
            _stack.remove(marker)
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        marker = id(value)
        if marker in _stack:
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "cycle": True}
        _stack.add(marker)
        try:
            return [_normalize_for_json(item, _stack) for item in value]
        finally:
            _stack.remove(marker)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        marker = id(value)
        if marker in _stack:
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "cycle": True}
        _stack.add(marker)
        try:
            return [_normalize_for_json(item, _stack) for item in value]
        finally:
            _stack.remove(marker)
    if isinstance(value, set):
        marker = id(value)
        if marker in _stack:
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "cycle": True}
        _stack.add(marker)
        try:
            normalized_items = [_normalize_for_json(item, _stack) for item in value]
            normalized_items.sort(key=_stable_sort_key)
            return normalized_items
        finally:
            _stack.remove(marker)
    if hasattr(value, "__dict__") and vars(value):
        marker = id(value)
        if marker in _stack:
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "cycle": True}
        _stack.add(marker)
        try:
            fields_map = {key: _normalize_for_json(val, _stack) for key, val in vars(value).items()}
            return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "fields": fields_map}
        finally:
            _stack.remove(marker)
    return {"__type__": _type_name(value), "repr": repr(value)}


def _label_for_path(value: Any) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, Path):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
        for key in ("name", "tool", "tool_name", "action"):
            raw = value.get(key)
            if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip():
                return raw
        return json.dumps(_normalize_for_json(value), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    if isinstance(value, SimpleNamespace):
        for key in ("name", "tool", "tool_name", "action"):
            raw = getattr(value, key, None)
            if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip():
                return raw
        return json.dumps(_normalize_for_json(value), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    if hasattr(value, "name"):
        raw = getattr(value, "name")
        if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip():
            return raw
    return str(value)


def _write_text(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def _write_bytes(path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(data)


def _write_json(path: Path, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")


@dataclass
class ReceiptWriter:
    """Write per-step receipts and raw payloads beneath a private audit root."""

    root: Path

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.root = Path(self.root)
        self.receipts_dir = self.root / "receipts"
        self.raw_dir = self.root / "raw"
        self.receipts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def record_step(self, step_idx: int, request: Any, response: Any, action: Any, raw_output: Any) -> Path:
        action_name = _safe_action_name(action)
        receipt_id = f"{step_idx:04d}_action_{action_name}"
        receipt_path = self.receipts_dir / f"{receipt_id}.json"
        raw_step_dir = self.raw_dir / receipt_id

        def write_raw_value(path: Path, value: Any) -> None:
            if value is None:
                _write_text(path, "")
                return
            if isinstance(value, bytes):
                _write_bytes(path, value)
                return
            if isinstance(value, bytearray):
                _write_bytes(path, bytes(value))
                return
            if isinstance(value, memoryview):
                _write_bytes(path, value.tobytes())
                return
            if isinstance(value, str):
                _write_text(path, value)
                return
            if isinstance(value, Path):
                _write_text(path, str(value))
                return
            if isinstance(value, (int, bool)) or (isinstance(value, float) and math.isfinite(value)):
                _write_text(path, str(value))
                return
            _write_text(path, json.dumps(_normalize_for_json(value), indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False))

        raw_payload: dict[str, Any]
        if isinstance(raw_output, Mapping):
            raw_payload = {}
            for key, value in raw_output.items():
                normalized_key = _normalize_key(key)
                raw_payload[normalized_key] = value
                write_raw_value(raw_step_dir / _safe_action_name(normalized_key), value)
        else:
            raw_payload = {"output": raw_output}
            write_raw_value(raw_step_dir / "output", raw_output)

        payload = {
--- runner/aether2/sessions.py ---
"""Tmux-backed session registry for persistent PTY interaction."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
import json
import shutil
import subprocess

from runner.aether2.executor import ContainerBackend


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SessionRecord:
    session_id: str
    command: str
    registry_path: str


class SessionRegistry:
    """Tmux-backed session registry (C1).

    When `backend.kind == "local"` (the default), `tmux` is invoked on the
    host exactly as before. When `backend.kind == "docker"`, every `tmux`
    invocation is routed through `docker exec <container> tmux ...` so the
    PTY session lives inside the task container, where the agent and verifier
    run. If `tmux` is unavailable in-container, callers get a truthful error
    (the same `RuntimeError("tmux is unavailable")` as the local case).
    """

    def __init__(self, state_dir: Path, *, backend: ContainerBackend | None = None) -> None:
        self.state_dir = state_dir.resolve()
        self.sessions_dir = self.state_dir / "sessions"
        self.sessions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.backend = backend or ContainerBackend()

    def start(self, session_id: str, command: str) -> str:
        self._require_tmux()
        path = self.sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
        if path.exists():
            raise ValueError(f"session already exists: {session_id}")
        self._tmux("new-session", "-d", "-s", session_id, command)
        record = SessionRecord(
            session_id=session_id,
            command=command,
            registry_path=str(path),
        )
        path.write_text(
            json.dumps(record.__dict__, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        return session_id

    def send(self, session_id: str, keys: str) -> None:
        self._require_tmux()
        self._load(session_id)
        self._tmux("send-keys", "-t", session_id, keys)

    def read(self, session_id: str) -> str:
        self._require_tmux()
        self._load(session_id)
        try:
            result = self._tmux("capture-pane", "-p", "-t", session_id)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
            stderr = (exc.stderr or "").strip()
            if "can't find" in stderr.lower() or "no such" in stderr.lower():
                return ""
            raise
        return result.stdout

    def stop(self, session_id: str) -> None:
        """Kill the underlying tmux session and remove it from the registry, if present."""
        self._require_tmux()
        path = self.sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            raise KeyError(f"unknown session: {session_id}")
        try:
            self._tmux("kill-session", "-t", session_id)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
            stderr = (exc.stderr or "").strip()
            if "can't find" not in stderr.lower() and "no such" not in stderr.lower():
                raise
        path.unlink()

    def list_session_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return sorted(path.stem for path in self.sessions_dir.glob("*.json"))

    def _load(self, session_id: str) -> SessionRecord:
        path = self.sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            raise KeyError(f"unknown session: {session_id}")
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return SessionRecord(
            session_id=str(data["session_id"]),
            command=str(data["command"]),
            registry_path=str(path),
        )

    def _require_tmux(self) -> str:
        if self.backend.kind != "local":
            # Existence is checked by actually invoking tmux in-container
            # (see _tmux); we cannot probe PATH from the host.
            return "tmux"
        tmux = shutil.which("tmux")
        if not tmux:
            raise RuntimeError("tmux is unavailable")
        return tmux

    def _tmux(self, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        tmux = self._require_tmux()
        if self.backend.kind == "local":
            command = [tmux, *args]
        else:
            if not self.backend.container_id:
                raise RuntimeError("docker backend requires a container_id")
            command = ["docker", "exec", self.backend.container_id, "tmux", *args]
        try:
            return subprocess.run(
                command,
                check=True,
                text=True,
                capture_output=True,
            )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
            stderr = (exc.stderr or "")
            if self.backend.kind != "local" and (
                "executable file not found" in stderr.lower() or "tmux: not found" in stderr.lower() or "no such file or directory" in stderr.lower()
            ):
                raise RuntimeError("tmux is unavailable") from exc
            raise

--- runner/aether2/tools.py ---
"""Generic provider tool schemas and dispatch helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

TOOL_NAMES: list[str] = [
    "run_command",
    "start_job",
    "job_status",
    "session_start",
    "session_send",
    "session_read",
    "read_file",
    "write_file",
    "wait",
    "task_done",
]


def _schema(name: str, description: str, properties: dict[str, Any], required: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": name,
            "description": description,
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": properties,
                "required": required,
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    }


TOOL_SCHEMAS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
    _schema(
        "run_command",
        "Run a foreground command in the task container and return its typed observation.",

            "cmd": {
                "type": "string",
                "description": "Shell command to execute in the task container.",

            "timeout_sec": {
                "type": "integer",

                "minimum": 1,
                "description": "Maximum runtime in seconds.",
            },

            "cwd": {
                "type": ["string", "null"],
                "description": "Optional working directory for the detached job.",
            },
        },

    _schema(

    _schema(

                "type": "string",
                "description": "Identifier for the persistent session.",

            "command": {

        ["session_id", "command"],

    _schema(

def dispatch(tool_name: str, args: dict[str, Any], ctx: Any) -> Any:
    """Dispatch a tool call to the matching method on ctx."""

    if tool_name not in TOOL_NAMES:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown tool: {tool_name}")
    handler = getattr(ctx, tool_name, None)
    if handler is None:
        raise AttributeError(f"context does not implement {tool_name}")
    return handler(**args)
--- runner/aether2/verify.py ---
"""Fresh-context verification and replay checks."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Mapping
import json

from runner.kernel_layer2_audit import _clean_hidden_refs


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckResult:
    command: str
    exit_code: int | None
    stdout: str
    stderr: str
    cwd: str
    duration_sec: float
    timed_out: bool = False
    error_kind: str | None = None
    error_reason_code: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RequirementResult:
    requirement: str
    verdict: str
    evidence: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DiscrepancyReport:
    requirements: tuple[RequirementResult, ...]
    reason_codes: tuple[str, ...]
    summary: str
    raw_response: str

    @property
    def has_discrepancies(self) -> bool:
        """True only when a requirement is positively `unsatisfied`.

        `unverifiable` verdicts are reported in `requirements`/`summary` for
        transparency but do NOT block finalization: the fresh-context
        verifier frequently cannot confirm interactive-session or
        background-job internals (it has no executor transcript access by
        design), so treating `unverifiable` as a discrepancy caused
        round-exhaustion on tasks that were in fact correct (anti-correlated
        with ground truth, per G2 fix-round-5 analysis).
        """
        if "verifier_parse_failed" in self.reason_codes:
            return True
        return any(item.verdict == "unsatisfied" for item in self.requirements)


VERIFIER_TOOL_SCHEMAS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "run_command",
            "description": "Run a read-only inspection command in the live task environment.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "cmd": {"type": "string"},
                    "timeout_sec": {"type": "integer", "default": 120},
                    "cwd": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
                },
                "required": ["cmd"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "read_file",
            "description": "Read a file from the live task workspace without modifying it.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "offset": {"type": ["integer", "null"]},
                    "limit": {"type": ["integer", "null"]},
                },
                "required": ["path"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "job_status",
            "description": "Inspect a detached job without modifying it.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"job_id": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["job_id"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "session_read",
            "description": "Read the current contents of a session without sending input.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"session_id": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["session_id"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
]


def replay_checks(checks: list[str], executor: Any) -> list[CheckResult]:
    results: list[CheckResult] = []
    for command in checks:
        raw = executor.run(command, timeout_sec=120, cwd=None)
        results.append(
            CheckResult(
                command=command,
                exit_code=_read_field(raw, "exit_code"),
                stdout=str(_read_field(raw, "stdout", "")),
                stderr=str(_read_field(raw, "stderr", "")),
                cwd=str(_read_field(raw, "cwd", "")),
                duration_sec=float(_read_field(raw, "duration_sec", _read_field(raw, "duration", 0.0))),
                timed_out=bool(_read_field(raw, "timed_out", False)),
                error_kind=_read_error_field(raw, "kind"),
                error_reason_code=_read_error_field(raw, "reason_code"),
            )
        )
    return results


def verify_fresh_context(
    task: str,
    orientation: Mapping[str, Any],
    diff: Mapping[str, Any],
    claim: Mapping[str, Any],
    checks_results: list[CheckResult],
    action_digest: Mapping[str, Any],
    model_client: Any,
    inspection_ctx: Any | None = None,
) -> DiscrepancyReport:
    clean_orientation = _strip_transcript_fields(_clean_hidden_refs(dict(orientation)))
    clean_diff = _strip_transcript_fields(_clean_hidden_refs(dict(diff)))
    clean_claim = _strip_transcript_fields(_clean_hidden_refs(dict(claim)))
    clean_checks = [
        _strip_transcript_fields(_clean_hidden_refs(result.__dict__))
        for result in checks_results
    ]
    clean_action_digest = _strip_transcript_fields(_clean_hidden_refs(dict(action_digest)))
    payload = {
        "task": task,
        "orientation": clean_orientation,
        "workspace_diff": clean_diff,
        "claim": clean_claim,
        "checks_results": clean_checks,
        "action_digest": clean_action_digest,
    }
    messages = [
        {
            "role": "system",
            "content": (
                "You are a fresh-context verifier. Evaluate the claim requirement by requirement, "
                "using only the provided task, orientation, workspace diff, replayed checks, and action digest. "
                "Do not assume access to any executor transcript.\n\n"
                "Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, using EXACTLY this schema "
                "(no other top-level keys are allowed):\n"
                "{\n"
                '  "requirements": [\n'
                '    {"requirement": "<short description of one task requirement>", '
                '"verdict": "satisfied" | "unsatisfied" | "unverifiable", '
                '"evidence": "<evidence for this verdict>"}\n'
                "    ... one entry per distinct requirement implied by the task ...\n"
                "  ],\n"
                '  "reason_codes": [<list of short machine-readable strings; empty list if no problems>],\n'
                '  "summary": "<one or two sentence overall summary>"\n'
                "}\n"
                'Do NOT use alternative keys such as "claim_satisfied", "verdict" at the top level, or "overall_evidence". '
                'Every requirement entry must use exactly the keys "requirement", "verdict", and "evidence", '
                'and "verdict" must be exactly one of "satisfied", "unsatisfied", or "unverifiable".'
            ),
        },
        {"role": "user", "content": json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)},
    ]
    response = _call_model(
        model_client,
        messages,
        VERIFIER_TOOL_SCHEMAS if inspection_ctx is not None else [],
    )
    messages_for_parse = list(messages)
    tool_calls = _extract_tool_calls(response)
    if inspection_ctx is not None and tool_calls:
        messages_for_parse.append(_assistant_message(response))
        for tool_call in tool_calls:
            tool_name = _tool_call_name(tool_call)
            if tool_name is None:
                continue
            arguments = _parse_tool_call_arguments(tool_call)
            handler = getattr(inspection_ctx, tool_name, None)
            if handler is None:
                continue
            result = handler(**arguments)
            messages_for_parse.append(
                {
                    "role": "tool",
                    "name": tool_name,
                    "tool_call_id": tool_call.get("id"),
                    "content": json.dumps(
                        _inspection_payload(result),
                        sort_keys=True,
                        separators=(",", ":"),
                        ensure_ascii=True,
                    ),
                }
            )
        response = _call_model(model_client, messages_for_parse, [])
    raw_text = _extract_text(response)
    parsed = _parse_report(raw_text)
    requirements = tuple(
        RequirementResult(
            requirement=str(item.get("requirement", "")),
            verdict=_normalize_verdict(str(item.get("verdict", "unverifiable"))),
            evidence=str(item.get("evidence", "")),
        )
        for item in parsed.get("requirements", [])
        if str(item.get("requirement", "")).strip()
    )
    return DiscrepancyReport(
        requirements=requirements,
        reason_codes=tuple(str(code) for code in parsed.get("reason_codes", [])),
        summary=str(parsed.get("summary", "")),
        raw_response=raw_text,
    )

  58: # Subprocess-spawn EAGAIN retry parameters (H1), matching
  59: # ContainerExecutor._run_subprocess's retry armor (5 attempts, 0.2s exponential
  60: # backoff) so verifier.sh invocations survive transient host fork pressure.
  61: _SPAWN_RETRY_MAX = 5
  62: _SPAWN_RETRY_BASE_SEC = 0.2

  65: class CleanupOutcome(NamedTuple):
  66:     log_lines: list[str]
  67:     blocked_homologs: dict[str, str]
  68: 
  69: 
  70: def _is_eagain_spawn_failure(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
  71:     if isinstance(exc, BlockingIOError):
  72:         return True
  73:     if isinstance(exc, OSError) and getattr(exc, "errno", None) == errno.EAGAIN:
  74:         return True
  75:     return False
  76: 
  77: 
  78: def _run_with_eagain_retry(
  79:     args: list[str], **kwargs: object
  80: ) -> tuple["subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] | None", str | None]:
  81:     """Run `subprocess.run(args, **kwargs)` with EAGAIN/fork-pressure retry.
  82: 
  83:     Returns (completed_process, None) on success, or (None, reason) if every
  84:     attempt failed due to host fork pressure (`fork: Resource temporarily
  85:     unavailable` / EAGAIN / BlockingIOError on spawn). Any other exception is
  86:     re-raised.
  87:     """
  88:     last_reason: str | None = None
  89:     for attempt in range(_SPAWN_RETRY_MAX):
  90:         try:
  91:             proc = subprocess.run(args, **kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
  92:         except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
  93:             if _is_eagain_spawn_failure(exc):
  94:                 last_reason = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
  95:                 time.sleep(_SPAWN_RETRY_BASE_SEC * (2**attempt))
  96:                 continue
  97:             raise
  98:         if proc.returncode == 128 and "fork: Resource temporarily unavailable" in (proc.stderr or ""):
  99:             last_reason = proc.stderr.strip()
 100:             time.sleep(_SPAWN_RETRY_BASE_SEC * (2**attempt))
 101:             continue
 102:         return proc, None
 103:     return None, last_reason or "fork: Resource temporarily unavailable (retries exhausted)"

 128:     existing = blocked_homologs.get(homolog_id)

 132: def _signal_and_wait_for_exit(pid: int, log: list[str], note: str) -> bool:
 133:     try:
 134:         os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM)
 135:         log.append(f"killed pid {pid} ({note})")
 136:     except ProcessLookupError:
 137:         return True
 138:     except OSError as exc:
 139:         log.append(f"failed to kill pid {pid} ({note}): {exc}")
 140:         return False
 141:     for _ in range(20):
 142:         try:
 143:             os.kill(pid, 0)
 144:         except ProcessLookupError:
 145:             return True
 146:         except OSError:
 147:             return True
 148:         time.sleep(0.1)
 149:     log.append(f"pid {pid} still alive after SIGTERM ({note})")
 150:     return False

 153: def _load_task(homolog_dir: Path, run_dir: Path) -> tuple[TaskSpec, int]:
 154:     instruction = (homolog_dir / "instruction.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 155:     config = json.loads((homolog_dir / "task.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 156: 
 157:     # H2(a): each run gets a FRESH, isolated workspace under
 158:     # runs/<ts>/workspaces/<homolog_id>/ rather than reusing the shared
 159:     # workspace/ dir in the homolog directory across runs. If the homolog
 160:     # ships a pristine fixture workspace (workspace_fixture/), seed from that;
 161:     # otherwise start empty (matching the previous rmtree+mkdir behavior).
 162:     workspace_root = run_dir / "workspaces" / homolog_dir.name / config["workspace_root"]
 163:     if workspace_root.exists():
 164:         shutil.rmtree(workspace_root)
 165:     fixture_dir = homolog_dir / "workspace_fixture"
 166:     if fixture_dir.exists():
 167:         shutil.copytree(fixture_dir, workspace_root)
 168:     else:
 169:         workspace_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

 174:     task = TaskSpec(
 175:         task_id=config["task_id"],
 176:         instruction=instruction,
 177:         task_dir=homolog_dir,
 178:         workspace_root=workspace_root,
 179:         artifacts_dir=artifacts_dir,
 180:     )
 181:     return task, int(config.get("time_budget_sec", 180))

 184: def _iter_prior_run_dirs(run_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
 185:     runs_root = run_dir.parent
 186:     return sorted(p for p in runs_root.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and p != run_dir)

 189: def _port_listener_pids(port: int) -> list[int]:
 190:     try:
 191:         proc = subprocess.run(
 192:             ["lsof", "-ti", f":{port}"],
 193:             capture_output=True,
 194:             text=True,
 195:             timeout=10,
 196:         )
 197:     except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
 198:         return []
 199:     pids: list[int] = []
 200:     for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():
 201:         line = line.strip()
 202:         if not line:
 203:             continue
 204:         try:
 205:             pids.append(int(line))
 206:         except ValueError:
 207:             continue
 208:     return pids

 211: def _cleanup_prior_runs(run_dir: Path) -> CleanupOutcome:
 212:     """H2(b): kill leftover processes from PRIOR G2 runs before starting.
 213: 
 214:     Two sources of evidence are used, and ONLY pids attributable to prior G2
 215:     runs (via pidfile path or matching cmdline) are killed -- never arbitrary
 216:     port holders:
 217: 
 218:     1. Job pidfiles under previous runs' `workspaces/<homolog_id>/.aether2/state/jobs/*/job.pid`.
 219:     2. `lsof -i :<port>` for each port a homolog task is known to use (e.g.
 220:        8123 for g2_02), cross-checked against the job pidfiles / cmdline so we
 221:        only kill processes whose cmdline matches the known job launch command
 222:        recorded in that job's meta.json `cmd`.
 223:     """
 224:     log: list[str] = []
 225:     known_pids: set[int] = set()
 226:     known_job_commands: dict[str, set[str]] = {key: set() for key in HOMOLOG_PORTS}
 227:     blocked_homologs: dict[str, str] = {}
 228: 
 229:     for prior in _iter_prior_run_dirs(run_dir):
 230:         for jobs_dir in prior.glob("workspaces/*/*/.aether2/state/jobs/*"):
 231:             pidfile = jobs_dir / "job.pid"
 232:             meta_cmd = _read_text_if_exists(jobs_dir / "meta.json")
 233:             if meta_cmd:
 234:                 try:
 235:                     cmd = json.loads(meta_cmd).get("cmd")
 236:                 except json.JSONDecodeError:
 237:                     cmd = None
 238:                 if isinstance(cmd, str):
 239:                     homolog_id = _homolog_id_from_path(jobs_dir)
 240:                     if homolog_id in known_job_commands:
 241:                         known_job_commands[homolog_id].add(cmd)
 242:             if not pidfile.exists():
 243:                 continue
 244:             try:
 245:                 pid = int(pidfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
 246:             except (ValueError, OSError):
 247:                 continue
 248:             if pid <= 0:
 249:                 continue
 250:             known_pids.add(pid)
 251:             _signal_and_wait_for_exit(pid, log, f"pidfile {pidfile}")
 252: 
 253:     # Also check legacy shared workspace/.aether2/state/jobs (pre-H2 layout).
 254:     for jobs_dir in HOMOLOGS_DIR.glob("g2_*/workspace/.aether2/state/jobs/*"):
 255:         pidfile = jobs_dir / "job.pid"
 256:         meta_cmd = _read_text_if_exists(jobs_dir / "meta.json")
 257:         if meta_cmd:
 258:             try:
 259:                 cmd = json.loads(meta_cmd).get("cmd")
 260:             except json.JSONDecodeError:

===== runner/aether2/executor.py =====
   1: """Workspace scoped foreground execution helper with optional container backing."""
   2: 
   3: from __future__ import annotations
   4: 
   5: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
   6: from pathlib import Path
   7: from time import perf_counter
   8: from typing import Any
   9: import errno
  10: import os
  11: import shlex
  12: import subprocess
  13: import time
  14: 
  15: from runner.aether2.envelope import ErrorInfo, FileDelta, ProcessDelta
  16: 
  17: 
  18: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  19: class RawResult:
  20:     tool: str
  21:     command: str
  22:     exit_code: int | None
  23:     duration_sec: float
  24:     cwd: str
  25:     stdout: str
  26:     stderr: str
  27:     workspace_root: str
  28:     timed_out: bool = False
  29:     boundary_violation: bool = False
  30:     files_changed: list[FileDelta] = field(default_factory=list)
  31:     process_delta: ProcessDelta = field(default_factory=ProcessDelta)
  32:     blind_retry_blocked: bool = False
  33:     error: ErrorInfo | None = None
  34: 
  35: 
  36: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  37: class ContainerBackend:
  38:     """Execution backend describing the live task environment."""
  39: 
  40:     kind: str = "local"
  41:     container_id: str | None = None
  42:     container_workspace_root: str | None = None
  43:     exec_shell: str = "sh"
  44:     base_env: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
  45: 
  46: 
  47: class ContainerExecutor:
  48:     """Run foreground shell commands with a workspace-root boundary."""
  49: 
  50:     def __init__(
  51:         self,
  52:         workspace_root: str | Path | None = None,
  53:         *,
  54:         backend: ContainerBackend | None = None,
  55:     ) -> None:
  56:         root = Path(workspace_root) if workspace_root is not None else Path.cwd()
  57:         self.workspace_root = root.resolve(strict=False)
  58:         self.backend = backend or ContainerBackend()
  59:         container_root = self.backend.container_workspace_root or self.workspace_root.as_posix()
  60:         self.container_workspace_root = self._normalize_container_root(container_root)
  61: 
  62:     @property
  63:     def execution_boundary(self) -> str:
  64:         return self.backend.kind
  65: 
  66:     def run(self, cmd: str, timeout_sec: int, cwd: str | Path | None = None) -> RawResult:
  67:         command = str(cmd)
  68:         started_at = perf_counter()
  69:         cwd_path, container_cwd, cwd_error = self._resolve_cwd(cwd)
  70:         if cwd_error is not None:
  71:             return self._finish_error(
  72:                 command=command,
  73:                 cwd_path=cwd_path,
  74:                 started_at=started_at,
  75:                 exit_code=2,
  76:                 timed_out=False,
  77:                 boundary_violation=cwd_error.kind == "workspace_boundary_violation",
  78:                 error=cwd_error,
  79:             )
  80: 
  81:         blocked_token = self._find_boundary_violation(command, cwd_path)
  82:         if blocked_token is not None:
  83:             return self._finish_error(
  84:                 command=command,
  85:                 cwd_path=cwd_path,
  86:                 started_at=started_at,
  87:                 exit_code=126,
  88:                 timed_out=False,
  89:                 boundary_violation=True,
  90:                 error=ErrorInfo(
  91:                     kind="workspace_boundary_violation",
  92:                     message=f"blocked path-like token outside workspace root: {blocked_token}",
  93:                     reason_code="workspace_boundary_violation",
  94:                     failure_class="path_visibility",
  95:                     details="heuristic workspace-root boundary guard",
  96:                     tool_name="run_command",
  97:                     command=command,
  98:                 ),
  99:             )
 100: 
 101:         try:
 102:             completed = self._run_subprocess(command, cwd_path=cwd_path, container_cwd=container_cwd, timeout_sec=timeout_sec)
 103:         except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
 104:             duration_sec = perf_counter() - started_at
 105:             stdout, stderr = self._normalize_timeout_streams(exc)
 106:             return RawResult(
 107:                 tool="run_command",
 108:                 command=command,
 109:                 exit_code=124,
 110:                 duration_sec=duration_sec,
 111:                 cwd=str(cwd_path),
 112:                 stdout=stdout,
 113:                 stderr=stderr,
 114:                 workspace_root=str(self.workspace_root),
 115:                 timed_out=True,
 116:                 boundary_violation=False,
 117:                 error=ErrorInfo(
 118:                     kind="timeout",
 119:                     message=f"command timed out after {timeout_sec}s",
 120:                     reason_code="timeout",
 121:                     failure_class="timeout",
 122:                     details="foreground command exceeded the configured timeout",
 123:                     tool_name="run_command",
 124:                     command=command,
 125:                     exit_code=124,
 126:                     timed_out=True,
 127:                 ),
 128:             )
 129:         except OSError as exc:
 130:             return self._finish_error(
 131:                 command=command,
 132:                 cwd_path=cwd_path,
 133:                 started_at=started_at,
 134:                 exit_code=71,
 135:                 timed_out=False,
 136:                 boundary_violation=False,
 137:                 error=ErrorInfo(
 138:                     kind="spawn_failed",
 139:                     message=str(exc),
 140:                     reason_code="spawn_failed",
 141:                     failure_class="runtime",
 142:                     details="foreground command could not be spawned",
 143:                     tool_name="run_command",
 144:                     command=command,
 145:                 ),
 146:             )
 147: 
 148:         duration_sec = perf_counter() - started_at
 149:         stdout = completed.stdout or ""
 150:         stderr = completed.stderr or ""
 151:         exit_code = int(completed.returncode)
 152:         error = None
 153:         if exit_code != 0:
 154:             error = ErrorInfo(
 155:                 kind="nonzero_exit",
 156:                 message=f"command exited with status {exit_code}",
 157:                 reason_code="nonzero_exit",
 158:                 failure_class="process_exit",
 159:                 details="foreground command completed but returned a non-zero exit code",
 160:                 tool_name="run_command",
 161:                 command=command,
 162:                 exit_code=exit_code,
 163:                 timed_out=False,
 164:             )
 165:         return RawResult(
 166:             tool="run_command",
 167:             command=command,
 168:             exit_code=exit_code,
 169:             duration_sec=duration_sec,
 170:             cwd=str(cwd_path),
 171:             stdout=stdout,
 172:             stderr=stderr,
 173:             workspace_root=str(self.workspace_root),
 174:             timed_out=False,
 175:             boundary_violation=False,
 176:             error=error,
 177:         )
 178: 
 179:     def resolve_workspace_path(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
 180:         resolved, error = self._resolve_workspace_path(path)
 181:         if error is not None:
 182:             raise ValueError(error.message)
 183:         return resolved
 184: 
 185:     def to_container_path(self, path: str | Path) -> str:
 186:         resolved = self.resolve_workspace_path(path)
 187:         relative = resolved.relative_to(self.workspace_root).as_posix()
 188:         if relative == ".":
 189:             return self.container_workspace_root
 190:         return f"{self.container_workspace_root}/{relative}"
 191: 
 192:     def _resolve_cwd(self, cwd: str | Path | None) -> tuple[Path, str, ErrorInfo | None]:
 193:         candidate = self.workspace_root if cwd is None else cwd
 194:         resolved, error = self._resolve_workspace_path(candidate)
 195:         if error is not None:
 196:             return self.workspace_root, self.container_workspace_root, error
 197:         if not resolved.exists() or not resolved.is_dir():
 198:             return (
 199:                 resolved,
 200:                 self._host_to_container_path(resolved),
 201:                 ErrorInfo(
 202:                     kind="cwd_missing",
 203:                     message=f"cwd does not exist or is not a directory: {resolved}",
 204:                     reason_code="cwd_missing",
 205:                     failure_class="filesystem",
 206:                     details="the resolved cwd must exist and be a directory",
 207:                     tool_name="run_command",
 208:                     command="",
 209:                     timed_out=False,
 210:                 ),
 211:             )
 212:         return resolved, self._host_to_container_path(resolved), None
 213: 
 214:     def _find_boundary_violation(self, command: str, cwd_path: Path) -> str | None:
 215:         try:
 216:             tokens = shlex.split(command, posix=True)
 217:         except ValueError:
 218:             return None
 219:         for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
 220:             if index == 0:
 221:                 continue
 222:             candidate = self._candidate_path_from_token(token, cwd_path)
 223:             if candidate is None:
 224:                 continue
 225:             if not self._is_within_workspace(candidate):
 226:                 return token
 227:         return None
 228: 
 229:     def _candidate_path_from_token(self, token: str, cwd_path: Path) -> Path | None:
 230:         if not token or token.startswith("-") or "://" in token:
 231:             return None
 232:         if not self._looks_like_path_token(token):
 233:             return None
 234:         resolved, error = self._resolve_workspace_path(token, cwd_path=cwd_path)
 235:         if error is not None:
 236:             return self._coerce_path(token).expanduser().resolve(strict=False)
 237:         return resolved
 238: 
 239:     def _looks_like_path_token(self, token: str) -> bool:
 240:         if token.startswith(("/", "./", "../", "~/")):
 241:             return True
 242:         if "/" in token:
 243:             return True
 244:         return Path(token).suffix.lower() in {
 245:             ".csv",
 246:             ".ini",
 247:             ".json",
 248:             ".jsonl",
 249:             ".log",
 250:             ".md",
 251:             ".py",
 252:             ".sh",
 253:             ".txt",
 254:             ".toml",
 255:             ".xml",
 256:             ".yaml",
 257:             ".yml",
 258:         }
 259: 
 260:     def _is_within_workspace(self, path: Path) -> bool:

  35: # Generic package-manager invocations (first 1-2 shell tokens). Used only to
  36: # detect "this run_command was a package install" for the §6.5 fact ledger's
  37: # `installed_packages` entry -- no task-specific package names or logic.
  38: _PACKAGE_MANAGER_PREFIXES: tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...] = (
  39:     ("apt-get", "install"),
  40:     ("apt", "install"),
  41:     ("pip", "install"),
  42:     ("pip3", "install"),
  43:     ("python", "-m", "pip", "install"),
  44:     ("python3", "-m", "pip", "install"),
  45:     ("npm", "install"),
  46:     ("npm", "i"),
  47:     ("yarn", "add"),
  48:     ("cargo", "install"),
  49:     ("gem", "install"),
  50:     ("go", "install"),
  51:     ("brew", "install"),
  52:     ("conda", "install"),
  53:     ("apk", "add"),
  54:     ("dnf", "install"),
  55:     ("yum", "install"),
  56: )
  57: 
  58: 
  59: def _is_package_manager_install(command: str) -> bool:
  60:     try:
  61:         tokens = shlex.split(command, posix=True)
  62:     except ValueError:
  63:         return False
  64:     for prefix in _PACKAGE_MANAGER_PREFIXES:
  65:         if tuple(tokens[: len(prefix)]) == prefix:
  66:             return True
  67:     return False

 110: class ExecutionContext:
 111:     """Adapts the container executor, job registry, and session registry to the dispatch surface."""
 112: 
 113:     def __init__(
 114:         self,
 115:         *,
 116:         executor: ContainerExecutor,
 117:         job_registry: JobRegistry,
 118:         session_registry: SessionRegistry,
 119:         raw_log_dir: Path,
 120:     ) -> None:
 121:         self.executor = executor
 122:         self.job_registry = job_registry
 123:         self.session_registry = session_registry
 124:         self.raw_log_dir = raw_log_dir
 125:         self.workspace_root = executor.workspace_root
 126:         self.last_snapshot: StateSnapshot = delta_snapshot(self.workspace_root)
 127:         self.last_delta_report = delta_diff(self.last_snapshot, self.last_snapshot)
 128:         # Cumulative run-level facts for the §6.5 fact ledger (not derivable from
 129:         # a single filesystem snapshot).
 130:         self.installed_packages: list[str] = []
 131:         self.nonzero_exits: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
 132: 
 133:     def run_command(self, cmd: str, timeout_sec: int = 120, cwd: str | None = None) -> ObservationEnvelope:
 134:         raw = self.executor.run(cmd, timeout_sec=timeout_sec, cwd=cwd)
 135:         exit_code = getattr(raw, "exit_code", None)
 136:         if exit_code == 0 and _is_package_manager_install(cmd):
 137:             self.installed_packages.append(cmd)
 138:         elif exit_code is not None and exit_code != 0:
 139:             self.nonzero_exits.append({"command": cmd, "exit_code": exit_code, "stderr": (getattr(raw, "stderr", "") or "")[-2048:]})
 140:         return self._observe_raw(raw)
 141: 
 142:     def start_job(self, cmd: str, job_id: str | None = None, cwd: str | None = None) -> ObservationEnvelope:
 143:         started_at = time.monotonic()
 144:         try:
 145:             resolved_job_id = self.job_registry.start(cmd, job_id=job_id, cwd=cwd)
 146:             status = self.job_registry.status(resolved_job_id)
 147:             raw = {
 148:                 "tool": "start_job",
 149:                 "exit_code": 0,
 150:                 "duration_sec": time.monotonic() - started_at,
 151:                 "cwd": status.cwd,
 152:                 "stdout": f"started job {resolved_job_id} (pid {status.pid})",
 153:                 "stderr": "",
 154:             }
 155:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - surfaced as a truthful error envelope
 156:             raw = _error_raw("start_job", exc, started_at=started_at, cwd=str(self.executor.workspace_root))
 157:         return self._observe_raw(raw)
 158: 
 159:     def job_status(self, job_id: str) -> ObservationEnvelope:

 209:     def session_read(self, session_id: str) -> ObservationEnvelope:
 210:         started_at = time.monotonic()
 211:         try:
 212:             screen = self.session_registry.read(session_id)
 213:             raw = {
 214:                 "tool": "session_read",
 215:                 "exit_code": None,
 216:                 "duration_sec": time.monotonic() - started_at,
 217:                 "cwd": str(self.executor.workspace_root),
 218:                 "stdout": screen,
 219:                 "stderr": "",
 220:             }
 221:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001

 224: 
 225:     def read_file(self, path: str, offset: int | None = None, limit: int | None = None) -> ObservationEnvelope:
 226:         started_at = time.monotonic()
 227:         try:
 228:             target = self.executor.resolve_workspace_path(path)
 229:             text = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
 230:             lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
 231:             start = offset or 0
 232:             if limit is not None:
 233:                 selected = lines[start : start + limit]
 234:             else:
 235:                 selected = lines[start:]
 236:             content = "".join(selected)
 237:             truncated_note = ""
 238:             if start > 0 or (limit is not None and start + limit < len(lines)):
 239:                 truncated_note = f"\n...[showing lines {start}:{start + len(selected)} of {len(lines)}]"
 240:             raw = {
 241:                 "tool": "read_file",
 242:                 "exit_code": 0,
 243:                 "duration_sec": time.monotonic() - started_at,
 244:                 "cwd": str(self.executor.workspace_root),
 245:                 "stdout": content + truncated_note,
 246:                 "stderr": "",
 247:             }
 248:         except ValueError as exc:
 249:             raw = _error_raw(
 250:                 "read_file",
 251:                 exc,
 252:                 started_at=started_at,
 253:                 cwd=str(self.executor.workspace_root),
 254:                 kind="workspace_boundary_violation",
 255:             )
 256:         except FileNotFoundError as exc:
 257:             raw = _error_raw("read_file", exc, started_at=started_at, cwd=str(self.executor.workspace_root), kind="file_not_found")
 258:         except OSError as exc:
 259:             raw = _error_raw("read_file", exc, started_at=started_at, cwd=str(self.executor.workspace_root), kind="io_error")
 260:         return self._observe_raw(raw)

===== runner/aether2/sessions.py =====
   1: """Tmux-backed session registry for persistent PTY interaction."""
   2: 
   3: from __future__ import annotations
   4: 
   5: from dataclasses import dataclass
   6: from pathlib import Path
   7: import json
   8: import shutil
   9: import subprocess
  10: 
  11: from runner.aether2.executor import ContainerBackend
  12: 
  13: 
  14: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  15: class SessionRecord:
  16:     session_id: str
  17:     command: str
  18:     registry_path: str
  19: 
  20: 
  21: class SessionRegistry:
  22:     """Tmux-backed session registry (C1).
  23: 
  24:     When `backend.kind == "local"` (the default), `tmux` is invoked on the
  25:     host exactly as before. When `backend.kind == "docker"`, every `tmux`
  26:     invocation is routed through `docker exec <container> tmux ...` so the
  27:     PTY session lives inside the task container, where the agent and verifier
  28:     run. If `tmux` is unavailable in-container, callers get a truthful error
  29:     (the same `RuntimeError("tmux is unavailable")` as the local case).
  30:     """
  31: 
  32:     def __init__(self, state_dir: Path, *, backend: ContainerBackend | None = None) -> None:
  33:         self.state_dir = state_dir.resolve()
  34:         self.sessions_dir = self.state_dir / "sessions"
  35:         self.sessions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  36:         self.backend = backend or ContainerBackend()
  37: 
  38:     def start(self, session_id: str, command: str) -> str:
  39:         self._require_tmux()
  40:         path = self.sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
  41:         if path.exists():
  42:             raise ValueError(f"session already exists: {session_id}")
  43:         self._tmux("new-session", "-d", "-s", session_id, command)
  44:         record = SessionRecord(
  45:             session_id=session_id,
  46:             command=command,
  47:             registry_path=str(path),
  48:         )
  49:         path.write_text(
  50:             json.dumps(record.__dict__, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
  51:             encoding="utf-8",
  52:         )
  53:         return session_id
  54: 
  55:     def send(self, session_id: str, keys: str) -> None:
  56:         self._require_tmux()
  57:         self._load(session_id)
  58:         self._tmux("send-keys", "-t", session_id, keys)
  59: 
  60:     def read(self, session_id: str) -> str:
  61:         self._require_tmux()
  62:         self._load(session_id)
  63:         try:
  64:             result = self._tmux("capture-pane", "-p", "-t", session_id)
  65:         except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
  66:             stderr = (exc.stderr or "").strip()
  67:             if "can't find" in stderr.lower() or "no such" in stderr.lower():
  68:                 return ""
  69:             raise
  70:         return result.stdout
  71: 
  72:     def stop(self, session_id: str) -> None:
  73:         """Kill the underlying tmux session and remove it from the registry, if present."""
  74:         self._require_tmux()
  75:         path = self.sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
  76:         if not path.exists():
  77:             raise KeyError(f"unknown session: {session_id}")
  78:         try:
  79:             self._tmux("kill-session", "-t", session_id)
  80:         except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
  81:             stderr = (exc.stderr or "").strip()
  82:             if "can't find" not in stderr.lower() and "no such" not in stderr.lower():
  83:                 raise
  84:         path.unlink()
  85: 
  86:     def list_session_ids(self) -> list[str]:
  87:         return sorted(path.stem for path in self.sessions_dir.glob("*.json"))
  88: 
  89:     def _load(self, session_id: str) -> SessionRecord:
  90:         path = self.sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
  91:         if not path.exists():
  92:             raise KeyError(f"unknown session: {session_id}")
  93:         data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
  94:         return SessionRecord(
  95:             session_id=str(data["session_id"]),
  96:             command=str(data["command"]),
  97:             registry_path=str(path),
  98:         )
  99: 
 100:     def _require_tmux(self) -> str:
 101:         if self.backend.kind != "local":
 102:             # Existence is checked by actually invoking tmux in-container
 103:             # (see _tmux); we cannot probe PATH from the host.
 104:             return "tmux"
 105:         tmux = shutil.which("tmux")
 106:         if not tmux:
 107:             raise RuntimeError("tmux is unavailable")
 108:         return tmux
 109: 
 110:     def _tmux(self, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
 111:         tmux = self._require_tmux()
 112:         if self.backend.kind == "local":
 113:             command = [tmux, *args]
 114:         else:
 115:             if not self.backend.container_id:
 116:                 raise RuntimeError("docker backend requires a container_id")
 117:             command = ["docker", "exec", self.backend.container_id, "tmux", *args]
 118:         try:
 119:             return subprocess.run(
 120:                 command,
 121:                 check=True,
 122:                 text=True,
 123:                 capture_output=True,
 124:             )
 125:         except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
 126:             stderr = (exc.stderr or "")
 127:             if self.backend.kind != "local" and (
 128:                 "executable file not found" in stderr.lower() or "tmux: not found" in stderr.lower() or "no such file or directory" in stderr.lower()
 129:             ):
 130:                 raise RuntimeError("tmux is unavailable") from exc
 131:             raise
 132: 

===== runner/aether2/jobs.py =====
   1: """Detached job registry for persistent background work."""
   2: 
   3: from __future__ import annotations
   4: 
   5: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
   6: from pathlib import Path
   7: from typing import Any
   8: import json
   9: import os
  10: import shlex
  11: import signal
  12: import subprocess
  13: import uuid
  14: 
  15: from runner.aether2.executor import ContainerBackend
  16: 
  17: 
  18: TAIL_LIMIT = 2048
  19: 
  20: 
  21: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  22: class JobStatus:
  23:     job_id: str
  24:     pid: int
  25:     alive: bool
  26:     exit_code: int | None
  27:     cwd: str
  28:     log_path: str
  29:     tail: str
  30:     registry_path: str
  31: 
  32: 
  33: class JobRegistry:
  34:     """Detached job registry. Jobs are launched through `backend` (C1): when
  35:     `backend.kind == "local"` (the default), the wrapper script is spawned on
  36:     the host exactly as before. When `backend.kind == "docker"`, the wrapper
  37:     script is launched INSIDE the task container via `docker exec -d
  38:     setsid ...`, so containerized tasks' services/jobs run where the agent
  39:     (and the verifier) actually live, not on the host. Pidfiles/logfiles/
  40:     registry state always live under `state_dir` (the task workspace's
  41:     `.aether2/state` dir), which is bind-mounted into the container, so
  42:     `status()` reads container truth either way.
  43:     """
  44: 
  45:     def __init__(self, state_dir: Path, *, backend: ContainerBackend | None = None, container_path_fn=None) -> None:
  46:         self.state_dir = state_dir.resolve()
  47:         self.jobs_dir = self.state_dir / "jobs"
  48:         self.jobs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  49:         self.backend = backend or ContainerBackend()
  50:         # Maps a host path to its in-container path string (required when
  51:         # backend.kind != "local"); injected by the caller (ExecutionContext),
  52:         # which already knows the workspace-root mapping.
  53:         self._container_path_fn = container_path_fn
  54: 
  55:     def start(self, cmd: str, job_id: str | None = None, cwd: str | Path | None = None) -> str:
  56:         command = str(cmd).strip()
  57:         if not command:
  58:             raise ValueError("start requires a non-empty command")
  59:         resolved_job_id = job_id or f"job-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
  60:         job_dir = self.jobs_dir / resolved_job_id
  61:         job_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  62:         cwd_path = Path(cwd or self.state_dir.parent).resolve()
  63:         log_path = job_dir / "job.log"
  64:         exit_code_path = job_dir / "exit_code"
  65:         wrapper_path = job_dir / "run.sh"
  66:         pid_path = job_dir / "job.pid"
  67:         meta_path = job_dir / "meta.json"
  68: 
  69:         wrapper_path.write_text(
  70:             "\n".join(
  71:                 [
  72:                     "#!/usr/bin/env bash",
  73:                     "set +e",
  74:                     f"cd {json.dumps(str(cwd_path))}",
  75:                     (
  76:                         "trap 'status=$?; "
  77:                         f"if [ ! -f {json.dumps(str(exit_code_path))} ]; then "
  78:                         f"printf \"%s\\\\n\" \"$status\" > {json.dumps(str(exit_code_path))}; "
  79:                         "fi' EXIT"
  80:                     ),
  81:                     f"bash -lc {json.dumps(command)} >> {json.dumps(str(log_path))} 2>&1",
  82:                     "code=$?",
  83:                     f"printf \"%s\\n\" \"$code\" > {json.dumps(str(exit_code_path))}",
  84:                     "exit \"$code\"",
  85:                     "",
  86:                 ]
  87:             ),
  88:             encoding="utf-8",
  89:         )
  90:         wrapper_path.chmod(0o755)
  91: 
  92:         if self.backend.kind == "local":
  93:             with (job_dir / "launcher.out").open("ab") as stdout_handle, (job_dir / "launcher.err").open("ab") as stderr_handle:
  94:                 proc = subprocess.Popen(
  95:                     [str(wrapper_path)],
  96:                     cwd=str(cwd_path),
  97:                     start_new_session=True,
  98:                     stdout=stdout_handle,
  99:                     stderr=stderr_handle,
 100:                 )
 101:             pid = proc.pid
 102:         else:
 103:             pid = self._start_in_container(wrapper_path, job_dir)
 104: 
 105:         pid_path.write_text(f"{pid}\n", encoding="utf-8")
 106:         meta_path.write_text(
 107:             json.dumps(
 108:                 {
 109:                     "job_id": resolved_job_id,
 110:                     "cmd": command,
 111:                     "cwd": str(cwd_path),
 112:                     "pid": pid,
 113:                     "log_path": str(log_path),
 114:                     "registry_path": str(meta_path),
 115:                     "exit_code_path": str(exit_code_path),
 116:                     "backend_kind": self.backend.kind,
 117:                 },
 118:                 indent=2,
 119:                 sort_keys=True,
 120:             )
 121:             + "\n",
 122:             encoding="utf-8",
 123:         )
 124:         return resolved_job_id
 125: 
 126:     def _start_in_container(self, wrapper_path: Path, job_dir: Path) -> int:
 127:         """Launch `wrapper_path` detached INSIDE the container (C1).
 128: 
 129:         Runs `docker exec <container> setsid <wrapper> & echo $!` via the
 130:         container's shell so the launched process is reparented to the
 131:         container's init and survives the agent process tree exiting, and
 132:         prints its in-container PID to stdout for liveness checks.
 133:         """
 134:         if self.backend.kind != "docker":
 135:             raise RuntimeError(f"unsupported non-local backend kind: {self.backend.kind!r}")
 136:         if not self.backend.container_id:
 137:             raise RuntimeError("docker backend requires a container_id")
 138:         if self._container_path_fn is None:
 139:             raise RuntimeError("docker backend requires a container_path_fn to map host paths into the container")
 140:         container_wrapper = self._container_path_fn(wrapper_path)
 141:         exec_cmd = [
 142:             "docker",
 143:             "exec",
 144:             self.backend.container_id,
 145:             self.backend.exec_shell,
 146:             "-c",
 147:             f"setsid {shlex.quote(container_wrapper)} </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $!",
 148:         ]
 149:         completed = subprocess.run(exec_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
 150:         if completed.returncode != 0:
 151:             raise RuntimeError(f"failed to launch in-container job: {completed.stderr.strip()}")
 152:         pid_text = (completed.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()[-1] if completed.stdout else ""
 153:         try:
 154:             return int(pid_text)
 155:         except ValueError:
 156:             raise RuntimeError(f"failed to parse in-container job pid from output: {completed.stdout!r}")
 157: 
 158:     def _pid_alive_for_backend(self, pid: int) -> bool:
 159:         if self.backend.kind == "local":
 160:             return _pid_alive(pid)
 161:         if not self.backend.container_id:
 162:             return False
 163:         completed = subprocess.run(
 164:             ["docker", "exec", self.backend.container_id, "kill", "-0", str(pid)],
 165:             capture_output=True,
 166:             text=True,
 167:             check=False,
 168:         )
 169:         return completed.returncode == 0
 170: 
 171:     def status(self, job_id: str) -> JobStatus:
 172:         meta_path = self.jobs_dir / job_id / "meta.json"
 173:         if not meta_path.exists():
 174:             raise KeyError(f"unknown job: {job_id}")
 175:         data = json.loads(meta_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 176:         pid = int(data["pid"])
 177:         exit_code_path = Path(data["exit_code_path"])
 178:         exit_code = _read_exit_code(exit_code_path)
 179:         process_alive = self._pid_alive_for_backend(pid)
 180:         if exit_code is None and not process_alive:
 181:             # The launcher process was terminated (e.g. by an external signal)
 182:             # before it could record its own exit status. Report a truthful,
 183:             # generic "terminated externally" code rather than leaving the
 184:             # job stuck in an "alive" state forever.
 185:             exit_code = 143
 186:         alive = exit_code is None and process_alive
 187:         return JobStatus(
 188:             job_id=job_id,
 189:             pid=pid,
 190:             alive=alive,
 191:             exit_code=exit_code,
 192:             cwd=str(data["cwd"]),
 193:             log_path=str(data["log_path"]),
 194:             tail=_read_tail(Path(data["log_path"])),
 195:             registry_path=str(meta_path),
 196:         )
 197: 
 198:     def as_dict(self, job_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 199:         return asdict(self.status(job_id))
 200: 
 201: 
 202: def _pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
 203:     try:
 204:         os.kill(pid, 0)
 205:     except ProcessLookupError:
 206:         return False
 207:     except PermissionError:
 208:         return True
 209:     return True
 210: 
 211: 
 212: def _read_exit_code(path: Path) -> int | None:
 213:     if not path.exists():
 214:         return None
 215:     try:
 216:         return int(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
 217:     except ValueError:
 218:         return None
 219: 
 220: 
 221: def _read_tail(path: Path) -> str:
 222:     if not path.exists():
 223:         return ""
 224:     data = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
 225:     return data[-TAIL_LIMIT:]

===== runner/aether2/mirror.py =====
   1: """No-delta progress mirror for Aether-2."""
   2: 
   3: from __future__ import annotations
   4: 
   5: from dataclasses import dataclass
   6: 
   7: from runner.aether2.delta import DeltaReport
   8: 
   9: __all__ = ["Mirror", "MirrorNote"]
  10: 
  11: 
  12: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  13: class MirrorNote:
  14:     """Factual no-delta observation surfaced to the model."""
  15: 
  16:     action_signature: str
  17:     streak: int
  18:     text: str
  19:     fuel_gauge_text: str | None = None
  20:     note_type: str = "no_delta_progress"
  21: 
  22: 
  23: class Mirror:
  24:     """Track identical zero-delta streaks and emit factual observations."""
  25: 
  26:     def __init__(self) -> None:
  27:         self._last_action_signature: str | None = None
  28:         self._streak = 0
  29: 
  30:     @property
  31:     def streak(self) -> int:
  32:         return self._streak
  33: 
  34:     def observe(
  35:         self,
  36:         action_signature: str,
  37:         delta: DeltaReport,
  38:         *,
  39:         established_facts: list[str] | None = None,
  40:         unused_affordances: list[str] | None = None,
  41:         fuel_gauge_text: str | None = None,
  42:     ) -> MirrorNote | None:
  43:         if action_signature != self._last_action_signature:
  44:             self._last_action_signature = action_signature
  45:             self._streak = 0
  46: 
  47:         if not delta.is_empty:
  48:             self._streak = 0
  49:             return None
  50: 
  51:         self._streak += 1
  52:         if self._streak == 3:
  53:             return self._build_note(
  54:                 include_fuel_gauge=False,
  55:                 established_facts=established_facts or [],
  56:                 unused_affordances=unused_affordances or [],
  57:                 fuel_gauge_text=fuel_gauge_text,
  58:             )
  59:         if self._streak == 6:
  60:             return self._build_note(
  61:                 include_fuel_gauge=True,
  62:                 established_facts=established_facts or [],
  63:                 unused_affordances=unused_affordances or [],
  64:                 fuel_gauge_text=fuel_gauge_text,
  65:             )
  66:         return None
  67: 
  68:     def _build_note(
  69:         self,
  70:         *,
  71:         include_fuel_gauge: bool,
  72:         established_facts: list[str],
  73:         unused_affordances: list[str],
  74:         fuel_gauge_text: str | None,
  75:     ) -> MirrorNote:
  76:         facts_text = ", ".join(established_facts) if established_facts else "none recorded"
  77:         affordances_text = ", ".join(unused_affordances) if unused_affordances else "none recorded"
  78:         text = (
  79:             f"Steps in this streak produced no state change. "
  80:             f"Already established: {facts_text}. "
  81:             f"Not yet tried: {affordances_text}."
  82:         )
  83:         return MirrorNote(
  84:             action_signature="" if self._last_action_signature is None else self._last_action_signature,
  85:             streak=self._streak,
  86:             text=text,
  87:             fuel_gauge_text=(fuel_gauge_text or "elapsed/remaining time") if include_fuel_gauge else None,
  88:         )

===== runner/aether2/envelope.py =====
   1: """Typed observation envelope helpers for continuous harness execution."""
   2: 
   3: from __future__ import annotations
   4:

  14: _HEAD_TAIL_LIMIT = 2048

  36:     services_exited: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

  55: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  56: class ObservationEnvelope:
  57:     tool: str
  58:     exit_code: int | None
  59:     duration_sec: float
  60:     cwd: str
  61:     stdout_head: str
  62:     stdout_tail: str
  63:     stderr_head: str
  64:     stderr_tail: str
  65:     truncated: bool
  66:     raw_log_path: str
  67:     files_changed: list[FileDelta]
  68:     process_delta: ProcessDelta
  69:     blind_retry_blocked: bool
  70:     error: ErrorInfo | None

  72: 
  73: def collapse_cr_ansi(text: str) -> str:
  74:     """Collapse ANSI escape noise and carriage-return rewrites to the visible final state."""
  75:     if not text:
  76:         return text
  77:     without_ansi = _ANSI_RE.sub("", text)
  78:     normalized = without_ansi.replace("\r\n", "\n")
  79:     rendered_lines: list[str] = []
  80:     current: list[str] = []
  81:     for char in normalized:
  82:         if char == "\r":
  83:             current.clear()
  84:             continue
  85:         if char == "\n":
  86:             rendered_lines.append("".join(current))
  87:             rendered_lines.append("\n")
  88:             current.clear()
  89:             continue
  90:         current.append(char)
  91:     rendered_lines.append("".join(current))
  92:     return "".join(rendered_lines)
  93: 
  94: 
  95: def build_envelope(raw: Any, *, raw_log_dir: Path) -> ObservationEnvelope:
  96:     tool = str(_coerce_field(raw, "tool", "unknown"))
  97:     exit_code = _coerce_optional_int(_coerce_field(raw, "exit_code", None))
  98:     duration_sec = float(_coerce_field(raw, "duration_sec", _coerce_field(raw, "duration", 0.0)))
  99:     cwd = str(_coerce_field(raw, "cwd", os.getcwd()))
 100:     stdout = str(_coerce_field(raw, "stdout", _coerce_field(raw, "stdout_text", "")))
 101:     stderr = str(_coerce_field(raw, "stderr", _coerce_field(raw, "stderr_text", "")))
 102:     files_changed = _coerce_file_deltas(_coerce_field(raw, "files_changed", []))
 103:     process_delta = _coerce_process_delta(_coerce_field(raw, "process_delta", None))
 104:     error = _coerce_error_info(_coerce_field(raw, "error", None))
 105:     blind_retry_blocked = _coerce_blind_retry_blocked(raw, error)
 106: 
 107:     raw_log_dir = Path(raw_log_dir).resolve()
 108:     raw_log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 109:     raw_log_path = raw_log_dir / f"{_slugify(tool)}_{uuid.uuid4().hex}.json"
 110:     raw_payload = {
 111:         "tool": tool,
 112:         "exit_code": exit_code,
 113:         "duration_sec": duration_sec,
 114:         "cwd": cwd,
 115:         "stdout": stdout,
 116:         "stderr": stderr,
 117:         "files_changed": [asdict(file_delta) for file_delta in files_changed],
 118:         "process_delta": _process_delta_to_dict(process_delta),
 119:         "blind_retry_blocked": blind_retry_blocked,
 120:         "error": None if error is None else _error_info_to_dict(error),
 121:     }
 122:     raw_log_path.write_text(json.dumps(raw_payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
 123: 
 124:     stdout_clean = collapse_cr_ansi(stdout)
 125:     stderr_clean = collapse_cr_ansi(stderr)
 126:     stdout_head, stdout_tail, stdout_truncated = _bound_stream(stdout_clean)
 127:     stderr_head, stderr_tail, stderr_truncated = _bound_stream(stderr_clean)
 128: 
 129:     return ObservationEnvelope(
 130:         tool=tool,
 131:         exit_code=exit_code,
 132:         duration_sec=duration_sec,
 133:         cwd=cwd,
 134:         stdout_head=stdout_head,
 135:         stdout_tail=stdout_tail,
 136:         stderr_head=stderr_head,
 137:         stderr_tail=stderr_tail,
 138:         truncated=stdout_truncated or stderr_truncated,
 139:         raw_log_path=str(raw_log_path),
 140:         files_changed=files_changed,
 141:         process_delta=process_delta,
 142:         blind_retry_blocked=blind_retry_blocked,
 143:         error=error,
 144:     )
 145: 
 146: 
 147: def _bound_stream(text: str) -> tuple[str, str, bool]:
 148:     length = len(text)
 149:     if length <= _HEAD_TAIL_LIMIT:
 150:         return text, "", False
 151:     if length <= _FULL_BOUND_LIMIT:
 152:         return text[:_HEAD_TAIL_LIMIT], text[_HEAD_TAIL_LIMIT:], False
 153:     return text[:_HEAD_TAIL_LIMIT], text[-_HEAD_TAIL_LIMIT:], True
 154: 
 155: 
 156: def _coerce_field(raw: Any, name: str, default: Any) -> Any:
 157:     if isinstance(raw, Mapping) and name in raw:
 158:         return raw[name]
 159:     if hasattr(raw, name):
 160:         return getattr(raw, name)
 161:     return default
 162: 
 163: 
 164: def _coerce_optional_int(value: Any) -> int | None:
 165:     if value is None:
 166:         return None
 167:     return int(value)
 168: 
 169: 
 170: def _coerce_file_deltas(value: Any) -> list[FileDelta]:
 171:     if value is None:
 172:         return []
 173:     deltas: list[FileDelta] = []
 174:     for item in value:
 175:         if isinstance(item, FileDelta):
 176:             deltas.append(item)
 177:             continue
 178:         if isinstance(item, Mapping):
 179:             deltas.append(
 180:                 FileDelta(
 181:                     path=str(item.get("path", "")),
 182:                     hash_before=_optional_str(item.get("hash_before")),
 183:                     hash_after=_optional_str(item.get("hash_after")),
 184:                     change_type=str(item.get("change_type", "unknown")),
 185:                 )
 186:             )
 187:             continue
 188:         deltas.append(
 189:             FileDelta(
 190:                 path=str(getattr(item, "path", "")),
 191:                 hash_before=_optional_str(getattr(item, "hash_before", None)),
 192:                 hash_after=_optional_str(getattr(item, "hash_after", None)),
 193:                 change_type=str(getattr(item, "change_type", "unknown")),
 194:             )
 195:         )
 196:     return deltas
 197: 
 198: 
 199: def _coerce_process_delta(value: Any) -> ProcessDelta:
 200:     if value is None:
 201:         return ProcessDelta()
 202:     if isinstance(value, ProcessDelta):
 203:         return value
 204:     if isinstance(value, Mapping):
 205:         return ProcessDelta(
 206:             started=[str(item) for item in value.get("started", [])],
 207:             exited=[str(item) for item in value.get("exited", [])],
 208:             log_growth={str(key): int(val) for key, val in value.get("log_growth", {}).items()},
 209:             jobs_started=[str(item) for item in value.get("jobs_started", [])],
 210:             jobs_exited=[str(item) for item in value.get("jobs_exited", [])],
 211:             sessions_started=[str(item) for item in value.get("sessions_started", [])],
 212:             sessions_exited=[str(item) for item in value.get("sessions_exited", [])],
 213:             services_started=[str(item) for item in value.get("services_started", [])],
 214:             services_exited=[str(item) for item in value.get("services_exited", [])],
 215:             job_log_growth={
 216:                 str(key): int(val) for key, val in value.get("job_log_growth", {}).items()
 217:             },
 218:             session_log_growth={
 219:                 str(key): int(val) for key, val in value.get("session_log_growth", {}).items()
 220:             },
 221:             service_log_growth={
 222:                 str(key): int(val) for key, val in value.get("service_log_growth", {}).items()
 223:             },
 224:         )
 225:     return ProcessDelta(
 226:         started=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "started", [])],
 227:         exited=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "exited", [])],
 228:         log_growth={
 229:             str(key): int(val) for key, val in getattr(value, "log_growth", {}).items()
 230:         },
 231:         jobs_started=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "jobs_started", [])],
 232:         jobs_exited=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "jobs_exited", [])],
 233:         sessions_started=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "sessions_started", [])],
 234:         sessions_exited=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "sessions_exited", [])],
 235:         services_started=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "services_started", [])],
 236:         services_exited=[str(item) for item in getattr(value, "services_exited", [])],
 237:         job_log_growth={
 238:             str(key): int(val) for key, val in getattr(value, "job_log_growth", {}).items()
 239:         },
 240:         session_log_growth={
 241:             str(key): int(val) for key, val in getattr(value, "session_log_growth", {}).items()
 242:         },
 243:         service_log_growth={
 244:             str(key): int(val) for key, val in getattr(value, "service_log_growth", {}).items()
 245:         },
 246:     )
 247: 
 248: 
 249: def _coerce_error_info(value: Any) -> ErrorInfo | None:
 250:     if value is None:
 251:         return None
 252:     if isinstance(value, ErrorInfo):
 253:         return value
 254:     if isinstance(value, Mapping):
 255:         return ErrorInfo(
 256:             kind=str(value.get("kind", "unknown")),
 257:             message=str(value.get("message", "")),
 258:             reason_code=_optional_str(value.get("reason_code")),
 259:             failure_class=_optional_str(value.get("failure_class")),
 260:             details=_optional_str(value.get("details")),

  56: def _get_value(run: Any, name: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
